test_policy.notes: Official SAT/ACT scores are optional for international freshmen. Scores can help for BSN Nursing (a 3.0 GPA with SAT 1130 and EBRW 550, versus a 3.5 GPA test-optional), merit scholarships and University Honors College admission.

requirements.portfolio: Fine/studio art majors submit a digital portfolio after applying; music majors must audition (online upload for most programs, in person for classical performance).
requirements.notes: Application fee $50 is the IPEDS 2024-25 figure (not restated on the pages reviewed). International applicants email secondary transcripts and diplomas (with notarized English translations) to international@wpunj.edu; the office converts foreign grades. Personal statement, resume and recommendation letters are optional unless the major requires them. Required high school units: English 4, math 3, lab science 2, social science 2, plus 5 additional. All new students take placement tests in reading, writing and math. The Common App was not confirmed on the pages reviewed.

deadlines.label: Priority deadline for Nursing (BSN), fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Nursing applications completed after Dec. 1 are considered on a rolling basis until capacity. Pages print no year; taken as fall 2027 entry.

deadlines.label: Merit scholarship consideration (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The international freshman page says Jan. 1; the international Deadlines page says 'February 1 - Merit Scholarship package deadline'. The earlier date is used here to be safe. No year is printed; taken as 2027.

deadlines.label: Regular deadline for fall 2027 admission
deadlines.notes: Freshman decisions are rolling; applications after June 1 are still handled on a rolling basis. Pages print no year; taken as fall 2027. Spring regular deadline is Dec. 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Waived for U.S. citizens and permanent residents, citizens of the listed English-proficiency waiver countries, graduates (or students) of high schools in the U.S. or those countries, and students of international schools following those systems. An English-medium-of-instruction letter on school letterhead with signature and seal is accepted for up to five years. All new students take placement tests, and non-credit remedial English may be assigned. The page describes no separate ESL or conditional-admission pathway.

english.notes: The page does not list the new 1-6 TOEFL scale.

cost.notes: Student Accounts 2026-27 full-time (12-19 credits) per semester: tuition $8,379 in-state and $13,692 out-of-state, plus $178 technology and $105 student government fees; annual figures are two semesters. International students pay the out-of-state rate before the Pioneer Award (about $8,500 off for undergraduates in 2026-27). Housing and board for 2026-27 were not found; IPEDS 2024-25 lists on-campus food and housing $16,240 and books $1,600.

aid.notes: The Pioneer Award gives new main-campus international students an 80% discount on the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition (about $8,500 for 2026-27, estimated; automatic, no application; renewable with full-time enrollment and a 2.0 GPA; needs a valid F-1/J-1 visa). The university also awards close to 2,000 merit scholarships a year to freshmen and transfers, and all admitted students are generally considered automatically, but no international-specific merit amounts are published. FAFSA applies to U.S. aid-eligible students only.

majors.notes: Fall start only; international students are admitted. Priority date Dec. 1; first consideration needs a 3.5 high school GPA test-optional (3.0 GPA with SAT 1130 and EBRW 550) and B or better in lab biology and chemistry.
Portfolio review is part of admission.
Audition is required; the audition is the most important factor for admission to the department.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is listed on the international pages reviewed.
